title: How Bubble Tea Got Its Bubbles

blanks.sentence: A familiar black tea drink contains a _____.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — Changing tea habits in Britain

blanks.sentence: Bubble tea often contains milk and _____, along with tapioca balls.
The drink was first invented in _____.
A visit to _____ introduced the inventor to iced milk tea.
Back in Taiwan, he found tapioca balls at a _____.
Media attention accompanied the drink's rapid rise in _____.
After reaching nearby countries, bubble tea spread _____.

multipleChoice.question: What broader change in tea drinking does the British example illustrate?
options: New teas have largely displaced black tea in Britain.
Traditional tea now tends to be served without milk.
New varieties have gained ground alongside a familiar style.
Cold tea is preferred mainly on hot summer days.

multipleChoice.question: Which aspect of bubble tea can customers choose for themselves?
options: The extra flavours mixed into it.
The starch used for the balls.
The firmness of the tapioca balls.
The original strength of the tea.

multipleChoice.question: What are the "bubbles" in bubble tea?
options: Air pockets produced when milk is shaken.
Pieces of ice that soften in the drink.
Drops of flavouring mixed into the tea.
Chewy balls made from tapioca starch.

multipleChoice.question: Why can bubble tea take on different added flavours?
options: Iced milk tea loses its flavour in warm weather.
Tapioca has little taste of its own.
The balls are sourced from local markets.
Tea tastes different after it is chilled.

multipleChoice.question: What helped turn the new drink into a wider tea trend?
options: Its inventor opened tea shops in neighbouring countries.
Its range of flavours drew immediate media interest.
Well-known visitors began coming to the inventor's shop.
Local markets began selling the drink in large quantities.

multipleChoice.question: What does the inventor's mention of his other products suggest about bubble tea's rise?
options: His other products had failed before bubble tea appeared.
He regarded this product as certain to lead the range.
He had designed the range to attract media attention.
He did not see this product's success as guaranteed.

multipleChoice.question: According to the discussion, what helped the drink gain fans beyond Taiwan?
options: People enjoyed its smooth, chewy quality after trying it.
People followed celebrity visits to shops in each country.
People valued its newness more than its taste.
People chiefly wanted its range of added flavours.

multipleChoice.question: What does the suggestion about Britain imply?
options: Familiar tea could recover its appeal without any change.
A fresh version of a familiar drink could appeal there.
British drinkers already favour the Taiwanese version.
Returning to an older recipe could renew interest.
